text:
maria (runtime): Heads up — after the canary we pushed this morning I'm seeing p95 host preparse CPU up ~30% and grpc writev tail latency spikes. Repro on canary cluster. Profiling attached below.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed for runtime-service rev f3a2 at 1623456700 :white_check_mark:

alex (infra): Can you paste the CPU flame sample / perf text? short thread is fine.

maria (runtime): here's the quick perf top sample (2s sampling) from the host preparse thread:
```
cpu%  symbol
18.3% tokenization::tokenize
12.1% grpc::writev
8.4% parse::proto_unmarshal
6.7% kvcache::lookup (miss path)
4.5% string::utf8_normalize
```
Most of tokenization hotness is in short requests (<=32 tokens).

ryan (ml): hmm — that pattern smells like kernel selection falling back to the long-seq path for a lot of short requests. If the kernel selector is using avg_seq across a batch it can pick the wrong kernel when there's skew. We should check kernel_choice_hist and seq_length_hist for the canary.

priya (sre): also noticed KV cache miss rate jumped ~3x on the same hosts when we flipped the preparse flag yesterday. If kvcache misses force re-tokenize or re-parse, that will amplify the tokenization CPU. Can someone dump kvcache hit/miss counters?

alex (infra): quick mitigation candidate — force small-sequence kernel for the canary path and increase kv shard window to reduce churn. Minimal config changes: 
```yaml
runtime.flags:
  KERNEL_OVERRIDE_SMALL_SEQ: 1  # force small-seq kernels for now
  KV_CACHE_SHARD_WINDOW: 128    # widen shard eviction window
```
Risk: small-seq kernel may be slightly less efficient for rare long sequences; acceptable for short canary.

maria (runtime): I'll try the kernel override + kv window on the next canary. Any thoughts about grpc writev spikes? looks like lots of tiny writes causing syscalls.

ryan (ml): batching heuristic tweak can help — current score is tokens_per_request which encourages many tiny requests to batch inefficiently. Prefer a score like tokens_per_request * sqrt(batch_size) or add a penalty for head-of-stream flushes. Pseudo: 
```py
def score(req, batch):
  return req.tokens * math.sqrt(max(1, len(batch))) - flush_penalty(req)
```
That biases towards forming slightly larger batches for many short requests and reduces writev churn.

devops-bot: Patch runtime-canary (f3a2 -> f3a3) deployed at 1623456800 with flags KERNEL_OVERRIDE_SMALL_SEQ=1, KV_CACHE_SHARD_WINDOW=128. Rolling canary.

priya (sre): please also enable http2 ingress write coalesce tracing (ingress.proxy.writev.coalesce=DEBUG) and sample window sizes. We've seen http2 window stalls amplify syscalls when small frames are common.

alex (infra): good call. I'll add a temporary tracepoint and a slim metric for small-write-counts per-second. If we see writev_count spike we can revert.

maria (runtime): thanks — running the canary now. Will post p95/p99 and kvcache hit rate after 15m. If numbers look good we'll push to staging. :thumbsup:
